source: National Archives Bill of Rights transcript, Amendment VII
review_notes: Codex reviewed the entire Seventh Amendment. The jury-trial preservation rule is conditioned on common-law suits above the stated amount. The re-examination rule carries its common-law exception; the dollar threshold is not copied onto that separate rule. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
Amendment VII

In Suits at common law, where the value in controversy shall exceed twenty dollars, the right of trial by jury shall be preserved, and no fact tried by a jury, shall be otherwise re-examined in any Court of the United States, than according to the rules of the common law.
